catalog.title: Agent Skill Catalog - Universal Application Creation, Software Engineering, and Delivery
preamble: AGENT SKILL
CATALOG
Universal Application Creation, Software Engineering, and
Delivery
30 categories - 244 proposed skills
Purpose
A comprehensive catalog for designing a modular agent that can plan, build, read, repair, transform,
test, package, and maintain applications in user-specified languages, frameworks, builders, IDEs,
runtimes, and target formats.
Design principle: Use focused, composable skills rather than one unlimited "knows
everything" skill. Each implementation should resolve the requested version, read authoritative
documentation when needed, work from actual files and tools, state capability boundaries, and
verify outputs before claiming success.
How to Use This Catalog
- Select the smallest set of skills that covers the user's request. Route by platform, language,
framework, version, artifact type, and delivery target.
- Implement each catalog item as a separate reusable skill or as a focused reference module under a
broader skill. Keep trigger descriptions precise to prevent unrelated activation.
- Do not bundle every historical and current document into a skill. Store compact version maps and
retrieve authoritative documentation for the exact version when the task requires it.
- Require executable checks for code and artifact claims: build, test, lint, render, package, reopen, or
run through the recipient's path whenever available.
- Compose app-building work through an app-factory workflow: requirements → architecture →
implementation → tests → security → documentation → packaging → release readiness.
Recommended Catalog Fields for Future Skill Creation
Field What to capture
Skill name Short, specific, lowercase package name and a
readable display name.
Trigger description What the skill does and the exact requests, files,
platforms, or situations that should invoke it.
Inputs Required files, repository, language, version,
target platform, credentials, data, and
constraints.
Outputs Exact artifact types, folder structure, source,
tests, documentation, packages, and reports.
Toolchain Compilers, SDKs, IDEs, package managers,
builders, emulators, devices, and external
services.
Version policy Supported versions, documentation source,
compatibility matrix, migration rules, and
forbidden version mixing.
Workflow Ordered build steps, decision points, fallback
paths, and handoffs to other skills.
Verification Build, test, security, accessibility, performance,
packaging, visual, and recipient-path checks.
Boundaries Unavailable hardware, credentials, licenses,
network access, store submission, or actions
requiring user approval.
Skill Catalog
The descriptions below define intended capability and execution scope. They are catalog specifications,
not claims that a single agent already possesses every tool, document, credential, compiler, device, or
service.

appendices.title: Recommended App-Factory Composition
items: Intake: Requirements-to-Backlog Engineer + Language and Framework Router
Design: Universal App Solution Architect + relevant platform architect
Build: Requested language, framework, builder, database, and integration skills
Verify: Test Strategy Architect + security + accessibility + performance skills
Deliver: Build-Run-Test Coordinator + Artifact Handoff and Packaging Manager
Operate: Observability Instrumentation Engineer + Site Reliability Engineer + Maintenance and Upgrade Planner

appendices.title: Non-Negotiable Execution Rules
items: Never claim a project builds, runs, passes tests, or is store-ready unless the corresponding check was actually completed.
Never mix syntax, APIs, build files, or documentation from incompatible versions. Resolve the target version first.
Preserve user code and edits. Make the smallest correct change and include regression coverage for repaired defects.
Use real project files and environments when supplied. Do not replace missing inputs with invented production data.
Return clean, editable source and exact build or run instructions. Include only requested artifacts in the final package.
Treat security, privacy, accessibility, licensing, and platform policy as design constraints, not optional final checks.
